metadata.note: The Somerset Railroad (1873-1884) and its reorganized successor the Somerset Railway (1884-1911), Oakland - Norridgewock - Madison - North Anson - Solon - Bingham with the 1905-07 Kineo extension from Austin Junction to Kineo Station on Moosehead Lake, and the same lines as the Maine Central's Kineo Branch 1911-1933. Drawn from research/branches/somerset_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-10-14; only the report's drawable spans are drawn, with era boundaries encoded as a shared year as in kennebec_and_portland_railroad.geojson. Rule 4: one Somerset feature per construction stage, plus two Maine Central features (trunk and extension) sharing that geometry from 1911. The 1884 reorganization is a foreclosure succession on the same line with no change of operator found, so it is a segment boundary, not a feature split. Not drawn (Rule 1): the Norridgewock quarry spur, the Bald Mountain logging branch, Deadwater/Lake Moxie sawmill sidings, the Madison paper-mill trackage, the Somerset Junction connecting curve to the Canadian Pacific (no passenger use), and all freight after 1933 (North Anson - Bingham to 1979, Oakland - Madison to 2013).

segments.note: Somerset Railroad era. Opened to Norridgewock in 1873 (en.Wikipedia; de.Wikipedia has the first trains through to Madison in 1873). A Bangor Daily News review and a Maine Memory exhibit say 1872 - seen only as search summaries, not used. The company defaulted in 1879; who ran the trains 1879-1884 (company, trustees or a receiver) is not found. End 1884 is an era boundary: the road was reorganized as the Somerset Railway in 1884 (en.Wikipedia; de.Wikipedia says only 'a few years' after the default) - the same line under a foreclosure successor, not a change of operator, so the colour does not change. First PRIMARY confirmation of passenger service is Fowler's 1892/94 MEC timetable letter (z). Headway is an estimate; no source gives a train count for this era.

segments.note: Maine Central operation from July 1911. The July 1911 Official Guide (p. 223, as cited by de.Wikipedia) shows two weekday trains and one Sunday train in summer; winter service was one weekday pair. Revenue fell from 1929; the whole line Austin Junction - Kineo Station closed 22 July 1933 and was dismantled (de.Wikipedia; en.Wikipedia: dismantled that year) - here passenger end and abandonment coincide. Every station Deadwater - Kineo Station carries Fowler letters a, b, c (1911, 1921, 1932). Headway is an estimate from the 1911 summer count.
